exposure: late preterm birth (34th-36th week of pregnancy)
cohort: All mothers and their late preterm infants (34+0 - 36+6 weeks) born in a tertiary referral academic center in 2010 and 2011
finding: A statistically significant relationship was found between respiratory distress syndrome and infant immaturity, poor condition after birth, and sepsis.
mod_finding: Sepsis was more common in the case of vaginal delivery and coexisted with respiratory distress syndrome, while perinatal asphyxia positively correlated with Caesarean section and respiratory distress syndrome after birth.
